LESSON_SIXTEEN_GRAMMAR_ONE.titleEnglish: Say How Close or Far Two Places Are with 離
LESSON_SIXTEEN_GRAMMAR_ONE.learnerPromise: Say how close or far one place is from another.
LESSON_SIXTEEN_GRAMMAR_ONE.explanation: 離 says the distance from one place to another. Put 很近 (very close) or 很遠 (very far) after the second place.

teachingGlossary.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
link word that connects a describing word to a thing
to have a holiday or vacation

LESSON_SIXTEEN_GRAMMAR_ONE.pattern: Place A + 離 + Place B + 很 (近／遠)

patternRows.english: The train station is very close to the department store.
The school is far from the hospital.
My home is very close to the park.

items.question: Can I say how far two places are without 離?
items.answer: No. 離 is the word that names the distance. Without it, the sentence does not compare two places.

right.traditional: 火車站離百貨公司很近。
right.simplified: 火车站离百货公司很近。
right.pinyin: huǒchē zhàn lí bǎihuò gōngsī hěn jìn。
right.english: The train station is very close to the department store.

items.question: What is the difference between 離 and 從?
items.answer: 離 tells a distance between two places. 從 tells where a trip starts. Use 離 for distance.

right.pinyin: xuéxiào lí yīyuàn hěn yuǎn。
right.english: The school is far from the hospital.

items.question: Where does 很近 go in the sentence?
items.answer: Right after the second place. The pattern is Place A 離 Place B 很近.
items.wrongTraditional: 離火車站百貨公司很近。
items.wrongSimplified: 离火车站百货公司很近。

right.traditional: 火車站離百貨公司很近。
right.simplified: 火车站离百货公司很近。
right.pinyin: huǒchē zhàn lí bǎihuò gōngsī hěn jìn。
right.english: The train station is very close to the department store.

examples.teachingNote: 離 names the distance from place A to place B.

text.traditional: 火車站離百貨公司很近。
text.simplified: 火车站离百货公司很近。
text.pinyin: huǒchē zhàn lí bǎihuò gōngsī hěn jìn。
text.english: The train station is very close to the department store.

examples.teachingNote: 很遠 goes at the end of the pattern.

text.traditional: 學校離醫院很遠。
text.simplified: 学校离医院很远。
text.pinyin: xuéxiào lí yīyuàn hěn yuǎn。
text.english: The school is far from the hospital.

examples.teachingNote: The places can be anything: buildings, parks, or home.

text.traditional: 我家離公園很近。
text.simplified: 我家离公园很近。
text.pinyin: wǒ jiā lí gōngyuán hěn jìn。
text.english: My home is very close to the park.

LESSON_SIXTEEN_GRAMMAR_TWO.titleEnglish: Say What Changed from Before with 本來 (原來) … 後來 …
LESSON_SIXTEEN_GRAMMAR_TWO.learnerPromise: Say how things were before and what changed.
LESSON_SIXTEEN_GRAMMAR_TWO.explanation: 本來 (or 原來) tells how things were at first. 後來 tells what changed after. The two parts work together to show a change.

teachingGlossary.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
link word that connects a describing word to a thing
to have a holiday or vacation

LESSON_SIXTEEN_GRAMMAR_TWO.pattern: S + 本來 + first part，後來 + changed part

complement.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

patternRows.english: At first he had no car. Later he bought one.

complement.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

patternRows.english: At first I wanted to see a movie. Later it rained.

complement.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

patternRows.english: We first had three dogs. Later we gave one to a friend.

items.question: Do 本來 and 原來 mean the same thing?
items.answer: Yes, for showing how things were at first. Use either one at the start of the changed story.

right.traditional: 他本來沒有車，後來買車了。
right.simplified: 他本来没有车，后来买车了。
right.pinyin: tā běnlái méiyǒu chē， hòulái mǎi chē le。
right.english: At first he had no car. Later he bought one.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

items.question: Do I keep 來 or 了 at the very end?
items.answer: The changed part ends with 了. 後來 sits before the changed part, not at the end.
items.wrongTraditional: 他本來沒有車，後來買車來。
items.wrongSimplified: 他本来没有车，后来买车来。

right.traditional: 他本來沒有車，後來買車了。
right.simplified: 他本来没有车，后来买车了。
right.pinyin: tā běnlái méiyǒu chē， hòulái mǎi chē le。
right.english: At first he had no car. Later he bought one.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

items.question: Can I use only 後來 to show a change?
items.answer: A change story reads better with both parts. 本來 (or 原來) starts it, and 後來 gives the change.

right.traditional: 他本來沒有車，後來買車了。
right.simplified: 他本来没有车，后来买车了。
right.pinyin: tā běnlái méiyǒu chē， hòulái mǎi chē le。
right.english: At first he had no car. Later he bought one.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

examples.teachingNote: 本來 starts the first plan; 後來 gives what changed.

text.traditional: 我今天本來想去看電影，後來下雨就沒去了。
text.simplified: 我今天本来想去看电影，后来下雨就没去了。
text.pinyin: wǒ jīntiān běnlái xiǎng qù kàn diànyǐng， hòulái xià yǔ jiù méi qù le。
text.english: I first wanted to see a movie today, but then it rained so I did not go.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

examples.teachingNote: 原來 works the same as 本來 here.

text.traditional: 我家原來有三隻狗，後來一隻送朋友了。
text.simplified: 我家原来有三只狗，后来一只送朋友了。
text.pinyin: wǒ jiā yuánlái yǒu sān zhī gǒu， hòulái yì zhī sòng péngyǒu le。
text.english: We first had three dogs; later we gave one to a friend.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

examples.teachingNote: The changed part ends with 了.

text.traditional: 他本來沒有車，後來買車了。
text.simplified: 他本来没有车，后来买车了。
text.pinyin: tā běnlái méiyǒu chē， hòulái mǎi chē le。
text.english: At first he had no car, so later he bought one.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

LESSON_SIXTEEN_GRAMMAR_THREE.titleEnglish: Compare Two Things as Even More with 更
LESSON_SIXTEEN_GRAMMAR_THREE.learnerPromise: Say that one thing is even more so than another.
LESSON_SIXTEEN_GRAMMAR_THREE.explanation: 比 compares two things. 更 makes the second thing stronger. The shape is: thing one + 比 + thing two + 更 + a describing word.

teachingGlossary.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
link word that connects a describing word to a thing
to have a holiday or vacation

LESSON_SIXTEEN_GRAMMAR_THREE.pattern: Thing one + 比 + thing two + 更 + describing word

patternRows.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.
Family is even more important than friends.
He is even smarter than I am.

items.question: Can I compare with only 更?
items.answer: For a two-thing comparison you also need 比. The shape is thing 比 thing 更 + describing word.

right.pinyin: jīntiān bǐ zuótiān gèng lěng。
right.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.

items.question: Where does 更 go?
items.answer: Right before the describing word. It is not after the second thing.

right.pinyin: jīntiān bǐ zuótiān gèng lěng。
right.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.

items.question: Does 更 mean the most?
items.answer: No. 更 means even more between two things. Say 最 for the most among a group.

right.pinyin: jīntiān bǐ zuótiān gèng lěng。
right.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.

examples.teachingNote: 比 shows the two things; 更 makes the second stronger.

text.traditional: 今天比昨天更冷。
text.simplified: 今天比昨天更冷。
text.pinyin: jīntiān bǐ zuótiān gèng lěng。
text.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.

examples.teachingNote: The comparing word is 更, not 很.

text.traditional: 我覺得家人比朋友更重要。
text.simplified: 我觉得家人比朋友更重要。
text.pinyin: wǒ juéde jiārén bǐ péngyǒu gèng zhòngyào。
text.english: I feel that family is even more important than friends.

examples.teachingNote: Any two people or things can be compared with 比 and 更.

text.traditional: 他比我更聰明。
text.simplified: 他比我更聪明。
text.pinyin: tā bǐ wǒ gèng cōngming。
text.english: He is even smarter than me.

questions.correctFeedback: Use 比 to show the two things.
questions.repairFeedback: Put 比 between the two things.

segments.hint: Use 更 before the describing word.

questions.correctFeedback: The describing word needs 更.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 更 before the describing word.

segments.hint: Use 比 between the two things.

questions.correctFeedback: Start the comparison with the two things.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 比 between the two things.

LESSON_SIXTEEN_GRAMMAR_FOUR.titleEnglish: Link Two Finished Actions with 就
LESSON_SIXTEEN_GRAMMAR_FOUR.learnerPromise: Say what happened right after an action was finished.
LESSON_SIXTEEN_GRAMMAR_FOUR.explanation: Finish one action (verb + 了) and add 就 before the next action. The next thing happens right away.

teachingGlossary.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
link word that connects a describing word to a thing
to have a holiday or vacation

LESSON_SIXTEEN_GRAMMAR_FOUR.pattern: First action (verb + 了) + just now + next action

subject.meaning: to have a holiday or vacation
ending word: something is done or has changed

complement.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

patternRows.english: As soon as his holiday began, he went traveling.

subject.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

patternRows.english: As soon as class ended, I went to talk with my friend.

subject.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

patternRows.english: As soon as you get home, call me.

items.question: Where does the first 了 go?
items.answer: Right after the first action. 就 comes before the next action.

right.pinyin: tā fàng le jià， jiù qù lǚxíng le。
right.english: As soon as his holiday began, he went traveling.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
ending word: something is done or has changed

items.question: Do I need 就 between the two actions?
items.answer: Yes. 就 is the word that links the finished action to what happened right after.

right.pinyin: tā fàng le jià， jiù qù lǚxíng le。
right.english: As soon as his holiday began, he went traveling.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
ending word: something is done or has changed

items.question: Do both actions need 了?
items.answer: The first action takes 了 to show it is finished. The next action may also end with 了.

right.pinyin: tā fàng le jià， jiù qù lǚxíng le。
right.english: As soon as his holiday began, he went traveling.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
ending word: something is done or has changed

examples.teachingNote: The first action is finished; 就 opens the next one.

text.traditional: 他上個月放了假，就去旅行了。
text.simplified: 他上个月放了假，就去旅行了。
text.pinyin: tā shàng ge yuè fàng le jià， jiù qù lǚxíng le。
text.english: As soon as his holiday began last month, he went traveling.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
ending word: something is done or has changed

examples.teachingNote: The finished action is 下課; the next is 練習說中文.

text.traditional: 昨天我下了課，就跟朋友練習說中文了。
text.simplified: 昨天我下了课，就跟朋友练习说中文了。
text.pinyin: zuótiān wǒ xià le kè， jiù gēn péngyǒu liànxí shuō Zhōngwén le。
text.english: As soon as class ended yesterday, I practiced Chinese with my friend.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
ending word: something is done or has changed

examples.teachingNote: 每次 (every time) makes the rule repeat.

text.traditional: 他每次放了假，就去旅行。
text.simplified: 他每次放了假，就去旅行。
text.pinyin: tā měi cì fàng le jià， jiù qù lǚxíng。
text.english: Every time his holiday begins, he goes traveling.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

LESSON_SIXTEEN_GRAMMAR_FIVE.titleTraditional: V + 得 + 補語 (狀態補語)
LESSON_SIXTEEN_GRAMMAR_FIVE.titleEnglish: Describe How an Action Turned Out with 得
LESSON_SIXTEEN_GRAMMAR_FIVE.learnerPromise: Say how well, happily, or thoroughly an experience went.
LESSON_SIXTEEN_GRAMMAR_FIVE.explanation: Attach 得 directly to an action verb to describe how it was done or the state resulting from it (e.g. 玩得很開心, 笑得好開心).

teachingGlossary.meaning: structural particle indicating manner or degree
ending word: something is done or has changed
link word that connects a describing word to a thing
to have a holiday or vacation

LESSON_SIXTEEN_GRAMMAR_FIVE.pattern: Subject + Verb + 得 + Degree / Result Complement

patternRows.english: I had a wonderful time on this trip.
Look, you are smiling so happily in the photo.
He drives very fast.

items.question: When do I use 的 vs 得?
items.answer: Use 的 to describe a noun (漂亮的風景). Use 得 right after an action verb to describe how it is done (玩得很開心).

right.pinyin: wǒ wán de hěn kāixīn.
right.english: I had a great time.

items.question: Where does 得 go if the verb has an object?
items.answer: Either repeat the verb (放假放得不久) or state the activity first as topic (這次放假放得不久).

right.traditional: 這次放假沒有上次放得那麼久。
right.simplified: 这次放假没有上次放得那么久。
right.pinyin: zhè cì fàngjià méiyǒu shàng cì fàng de nàme jiǔ.
right.english: This vacation is not as long as the last one.

examples.teachingNote: 玩得很開心 describes the fun mood of the trip.

text.traditional: 我玩得很開心，可是旅館有點問題。
text.simplified: 我玩得很开心，可是旅馆有点问题。
text.pinyin: wǒ wán de hěn kāixīn, kěshì lǚguǎn yǒudiǎn wèntí.
text.english: I had a great time, but there was a minor issue with the hotel.

examples.teachingNote: 笑得好開心 describes a happy expression in photos.

text.traditional: 你笑得好開心，風景真漂亮！
text.simplified: 你笑得好开心，风景真漂亮！
text.pinyin: nǐ xiào de hǎo kāixīn, fēngjǐng zhēn piàoliang!
text.english: You're smiling so happily, and the scenery is truly beautiful!

examples.teachingNote: 放得那麼久 compares duration with an action complement.

text.traditional: 這次放假，沒有上次放得那麼久。
text.simplified: 这次放假，没有上次放得那么久。
text.pinyin: zhè cì fàngjià, méiyǒu shàng cì fàng de nàme jiǔ.
text.english: This break is not as long as the last one.

examples.teachingNote: 游得最快 from the zodiac story describes swimming performance.

text.traditional: 看誰游得最快，第一個到。
text.simplified: 看谁游得最快，第一个到。
text.pinyin: kàn shéi yóu de zuì kuài, dì yī ge dào.
text.english: See who swims the fastest and arrives first.

dialogue.title: 在台灣旅行 · Traveling in Taiwan

text.traditional: 國安，這次學校放假，你有什麼計畫？
text.simplified: 國安，這次學校放假，你有什麼計畫？
text.pinyin: Guó'ān, zhè cì xuéxiào fàngjià, nǐ yǒu shénme jìhuà?
text.english: Guo'an, school is going on vacation this time. Do you have any plans?

text.traditional: 我還沒打算要做什麼。這次放假，沒有上次放得那麼久，只放三天假，我不知道去哪裡比較好。
text.simplified: 我還沒打算要做什麼。這次放假，沒有上次放得那麼久，只放三天假，我不知道去哪裡比較好。
text.pinyin: Wǒ hái méi dǎsuàn yào zuò shénme. Zhè cì fàngjià, méiyǒu shàng cì fàng de nàme jiǔ, zhǐ fàng sān tiān jià, wǒ bù zhīdào qù nǎlǐ bǐjiào hǎo.
text.english: I haven't decided what to do yet. This break is not as long as the last one—only three days—so I don't know where it's best to go.

text.traditional: 我覺得太魯閣不錯，有山又有河。
text.simplified: 我覺得太魯閣不錯，有山又有河。
text.pinyin: Wǒ juéde Tàilǔgé búcuò, yǒu shān yòu yǒu hé.
text.english: I think Taroko Gorge is great; it has both mountains and rivers.

text.traditional: 在哪裡？離台北遠不遠？
text.simplified: 在哪裡？離台北遠不遠？
text.pinyin: Zài nǎlǐ? Lí Táiběi yuǎn bù yuǎn?
text.english: Where is it? Is it far from Taipei?

text.traditional: 在花蓮。花蓮在台灣東部，離台北有點遠，你可以坐火車去，也可以開車去，差不多四個小時。
text.simplified: 在花蓮。花蓮在台灣東部，離台北有點遠，你可以坐火車去，也可以開車去，差不多四個小時。
text.pinyin: Zài Huālián. Huālián zài Táiwān dōngbù, lí Táiběi yǒudiǎn yuǎn, nǐ kěyǐ zuò huǒchē qù, yě kěyǐ kāichē qù, chàbùduō sì ge xiǎoshí.
text.english: It's in Hualien. Hualien is in eastern Taiwan, somewhat far from Taipei. You can take a train or drive there; it takes about four hours.

text.traditional: 你去過嗎？
text.simplified: 你去過嗎？
text.pinyin: Nǐ qù guò ma?
text.english: Have you been there?

text.traditional: 我小學六年級的時候去過，我很喜歡那裡。
text.simplified: 我小學六年級的時候去過，我很喜歡那裡。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎoxué liù niánjí de shíhou qù guò, wǒ hěn xǐhuān nàlǐ.
text.english: I went when I was in sixth grade of elementary school. I liked it very much.

text.traditional: 那你打算去哪裡玩？
text.simplified: 那你打算去哪裡玩？
text.pinyin: Nà nǐ dǎsuàn qù nǎlǐ wán?
text.english: Where do you plan to go for fun?

text.traditional: 我想去合歡山。報紙上寫，這幾天可能會下雪。
text.simplified: 我想去合歡山。報紙上寫，這幾天可能會下雪。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù Héhuān Shān. Bàozhǐ shàng xiě, zhè jǐ tiān kěnéng huì xiàxuě.
text.english: I want to go to Hehuanshan. The newspaper says it might snow these few days.

text.traditional: 下雪？我還沒看過雪，合歡山在哪裡？
text.simplified: 下雪？我還沒看過雪，合歡山在哪裡？
text.pinyin: Xiàxuě? Wǒ hái méi kàn guò xuě, Héhuān Shān zài nǎlǐ?
text.english: Snow? I haven't seen snow before. Where is Hehuanshan?

text.traditional: 在台灣的中部，日月潭也在附近。
text.simplified: 在台灣的中部，日月潭也在附近。
text.pinyin: Zài Táiwān de zhōngbù, Rìyuè Tán yě zài fùjìn.
text.english: In central Taiwan. Sun Moon Lake is also nearby.

text.traditional: 日月潭很有名，我在書上看過，離合歡山近嗎？
text.simplified: 日月潭很有名，我在書上看過，離合歡山近嗎？
text.pinyin: Rìyuè Tán hěn yǒumíng, wǒ zài shū shàng kàn guò, lí Héhuān Shān jìn ma?
text.english: Sun Moon Lake is very famous. I read about it in a book. Is it close to Hehuanshan?

text.traditional: 不遠，我想去玩三天兩夜，先去日月潭，再去合歡山。
text.simplified: 不遠，我想去玩三天兩夜，先去日月潭，再去合歡山。
text.pinyin: Bù yuǎn, wǒ xiǎng qù wán sān tiān liǎng yè, xiān qù Rìyuè Tán, zài qù Héhuān Shān.
text.english: Not far. I want to go for three days and two nights: go to Sun Moon Lake first, and then to Hehuanshan.

text.traditional: 你記得多照一些相片給我看！
text.simplified: 你記得多照一些相片給我看！
text.pinyin: Nǐ jìdé duō zhào yìxiē xiàngpiàn gěi wǒ kàn!
text.english: Remember to take more pictures for me to see!

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Say What Changed from Before with 本來 (原來) … 後來 …
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say how things were before and what changed.
grammarPages.explanation: 本來 (or 原來) tells how things were at first. 後來 tells what changed after. The two parts work together to show a change.

teachingGlossary.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
link word that connects a describing word to a thing
to have a holiday or vacation

grammarPages.pattern: S + 本來 + first part，後來 + changed part

complement.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

patternRows.english: At first he had no car. Later he bought one.

complement.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

patternRows.english: At first I wanted to see a movie. Later it rained.

complement.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

patternRows.english: We first had three dogs. Later we gave one to a friend.

items.question: Do 本來 and 原來 mean the same thing?
items.answer: Yes, for showing how things were at first. Use either one at the start of the changed story.

right.traditional: 他本來沒有車，後來買車了。
right.simplified: 他本来没有车，后来买车了。
right.pinyin: tā běnlái méiyǒu chē， hòulái mǎi chē le。
right.english: At first he had no car. Later he bought one.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

items.question: Do I keep 來 or 了 at the very end?
items.answer: The changed part ends with 了. 後來 sits before the changed part, not at the end.
items.wrongTraditional: 他本來沒有車，後來買車來。
items.wrongSimplified: 他本来没有车，后来买车来。

right.traditional: 他本來沒有車，後來買車了。
right.simplified: 他本来没有车，后来买车了。
right.pinyin: tā běnlái méiyǒu chē， hòulái mǎi chē le。
right.english: At first he had no car. Later he bought one.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

items.question: Can I use only 後來 to show a change?
items.answer: A change story reads better with both parts. 本來 (or 原來) starts it, and 後來 gives the change.

right.traditional: 他本來沒有車，後來買車了。
right.simplified: 他本来没有车，后来买车了。
right.pinyin: tā běnlái méiyǒu chē， hòulái mǎi chē le。
right.english: At first he had no car. Later he bought one.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

examples.teachingNote: 本來 starts the first plan; 後來 gives what changed.

text.traditional: 我今天本來想去看電影，後來下雨就沒去了。
text.simplified: 我今天本来想去看电影，后来下雨就没去了。
text.pinyin: wǒ jīntiān běnlái xiǎng qù kàn diànyǐng， hòulái xià yǔ jiù méi qù le。
text.english: I first wanted to see a movie today, but then it rained so I did not go.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

examples.teachingNote: 原來 works the same as 本來 here.

text.traditional: 我家原來有三隻狗，後來一隻送朋友了。
text.simplified: 我家原来有三只狗，后来一只送朋友了。
text.pinyin: wǒ jiā yuánlái yǒu sān zhī gǒu， hòulái yì zhī sòng péngyǒu le。
text.english: We first had three dogs; later we gave one to a friend.

text.simplified: 他本来没有车，后来买车了。
text.pinyin: tā běnlái méiyǒu chē， hòulái mǎi chē le。
text.english: At first he had no car, so later he bought one.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Compare Two Things as Even More with 更
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that one thing is even more so than another.
grammarPages.explanation: 比 compares two things. 更 makes the second thing stronger. The shape is: thing one + 比 + thing two + 更 + a describing word.

teachingGlossary.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
link word that connects a describing word to a thing
to have a holiday or vacation

grammarPages.pattern: Thing one + 比 + thing two + 更 + describing word

patternRows.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.
Family is even more important than friends.
He is even smarter than I am.

items.question: Can I compare with only 更?
items.answer: For a two-thing comparison you also need 比. The shape is thing 比 thing 更 + describing word.

right.pinyin: jīntiān bǐ zuótiān gèng lěng。
right.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.

items.question: Where does 更 go?
items.answer: Right before the describing word. It is not after the second thing.

right.pinyin: jīntiān bǐ zuótiān gèng lěng。
right.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.

items.question: Does 更 mean the most?
items.answer: No. 更 means even more between two things. Say 最 for the most among a group.

right.pinyin: jīntiān bǐ zuótiān gèng lěng。
right.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.

examples.teachingNote: 比 shows the two things; 更 makes the second stronger.

text.traditional: 今天比昨天更冷。
text.simplified: 今天比昨天更冷。
text.pinyin: jīntiān bǐ zuótiān gèng lěng。
text.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.

examples.teachingNote: The comparing word is 更, not 很.

text.traditional: 我覺得家人比朋友更重要。
text.simplified: 我觉得家人比朋友更重要。
text.pinyin: wǒ juéde jiārén bǐ péngyǒu gèng zhòngyào。
text.english: I feel that family is even more important than friends.

examples.teachingNote: Any two people or things can be compared with 比 and 更.

text.traditional: 他比我更聰明。
text.simplified: 他比我更聪明。
text.pinyin: tā bǐ wǒ gèng cōngming。
text.english: He is even smarter than me.

questions.correctFeedback: Use 比 to show the two things.
questions.repairFeedback: Put 比 between the two things.

segments.hint: Use 更 before the describing word.

questions.correctFeedback: The describing word needs 更.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 更 before the describing word.

segments.hint: Use 比 between the two things.

questions.correctFeedback: Start the comparison with the two things.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 比 between the two things.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Link Two Finished Actions with 就
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say what happened right after an action was finished.
grammarPages.explanation: Finish one action (verb + 了) and add 就 before the next action. The next thing happens right away.

teachingGlossary.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
link word that connects a describing word to a thing
to have a holiday or vacation

grammarPages.pattern: First action (verb + 了) + just now + next action

subject.meaning: to have a holiday or vacation
ending word: something is done or has changed

complement.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

patternRows.english: As soon as his holiday began, he went traveling.

subject.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

patternRows.english: As soon as class ended, I went to talk with my friend.

subject.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

patternRows.english: As soon as you get home, call me.

items.question: Where does the first 了 go?
items.answer: Right after the first action. 就 comes before the next action.

right.pinyin: tā fàng le jià， jiù qù lǚxíng le。
right.english: As soon as his holiday began, he went traveling.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
ending word: something is done or has changed

items.question: Do I need 就 between the two actions?
items.answer: Yes. 就 is the word that links the finished action to what happened right after.

right.pinyin: tā fàng le jià， jiù qù lǚxíng le。
right.english: As soon as his holiday began, he went traveling.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
ending word: something is done or has changed

items.question: Do both actions need 了?
items.answer: The first action takes 了 to show it is finished. The next action may also end with 了.

right.pinyin: tā fàng le jià， jiù qù lǚxíng le。
right.english: As soon as his holiday began, he went traveling.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
ending word: something is done or has changed

examples.teachingNote: The first action is finished; 就 opens the next one.

text.traditional: 他上個月放了假，就去旅行了。
text.simplified: 他上个月放了假，就去旅行了。
text.pinyin: tā shàng ge yuè fàng le jià， jiù qù lǚxíng le。
text.english: As soon as his holiday began last month, he went traveling.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

text.simplified: 昨天我下了课，就跟朋友练习说中文了。

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
ending word: something is done or has changed

examples.teachingNote: 每次 (every time) makes the rule repeat.

grammarPages.titleTraditional: V + 得 + 補語 (狀態補語)
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Describe How an Action Turned Out with 得
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say how well, happily, or thoroughly an experience went.
grammarPages.explanation: Attach 得 directly to an action verb to describe how it was done or the state resulting from it (e.g. 玩得很開心, 笑得好開心).

teachingGlossary.meaning: structural particle indicating manner or degree
ending word: something is done or has changed
link word that connects a describing word to a thing
to have a holiday or vacation

grammarPages.pattern: Subject + Verb + 得 + Degree / Result Complement

patternRows.english: I had a wonderful time on this trip.
Look, you are smiling so happily in the photo.
He drives very fast.

items.question: When do I use 的 vs 得?
items.answer: Use 的 to describe a noun (漂亮的風景). Use 得 right after an action verb to describe how it is done (玩得很開心).

right.pinyin: wǒ wán de hěn kāixīn.
right.english: I had a great time.

items.question: Where does 得 go if the verb has an object?
items.answer: Either repeat the verb (放假放得不久) or state the activity first as topic (這次放假放得不久).

right.traditional: 這次放假沒有上次放得那麼久。
right.simplified: 这次放假没有上次放得那么久。
right.pinyin: zhè cì fàngjià méiyǒu shàng cì fàng de nàme jiǔ.
right.english: This vacation is not as long as the last one.

examples.teachingNote: 玩得很開心 describes the fun mood of the trip.

text.traditional: 我玩得很開心，可是旅館有點問題。
text.simplified: 我玩得很开心，可是旅馆有点问题。
text.pinyin: wǒ wán de hěn kāixīn, kěshì lǚguǎn yǒudiǎn wèntí.
text.english: I had a great time, but there was a minor issue with the hotel.

examples.teachingNote: 笑得好開心 describes a happy expression in photos.

text.traditional: 你笑得好開心，風景真漂亮！
text.simplified: 你笑得好开心，风景真漂亮！
text.pinyin: nǐ xiào de hǎo kāixīn, fēngjǐng zhēn piàoliang!
text.english: You're smiling so happily, and the scenery is truly beautiful!

examples.teachingNote: 放得那麼久 compares duration with an action complement.

text.traditional: 這次放假，沒有上次放得那麼久。
text.simplified: 这次放假，没有上次放得那么久。
text.pinyin: zhè cì fàngjià, méiyǒu shàng cì fàng de nàme jiǔ.
text.english: This break is not as long as the last one.

examples.teachingNote: 游得最快 from the zodiac story describes swimming performance.

text.traditional: 看誰游得最快，第一個到。
text.simplified: 看谁游得最快，第一个到。
text.pinyin: kàn shéi yóu de zuì kuài, dì yī ge dào.
text.english: See who swims the fastest and arrives first.

dialogue.title: 在台灣旅行 · Traveling in Taiwan

text.traditional: 放假的時候，你去太魯閣了嗎？
text.simplified: 放假的時候，你去太魯閣了嗎？
text.pinyin: Fàngjià de shíhou, nǐ qù Tàilǔgé le ma?
text.english: Did you go to Taroko during the vacation?

text.traditional: 我本來要去那裡，可是因為沒有車票了，所以後來決定去高雄玩。
text.simplified: 我本來要去那裡，可是因為沒有車票了，所以後來決定去高雄玩。
text.pinyin: Wǒ běnlái yào qù nàlǐ, kěshì yīnwèi méiyǒu chēpiào le, suǒyǐ hòulái juédìng qù Gāoxióng wán.
text.english: I originally intended to go there, but because there were no more train tickets, I later decided to go to Kaohsiung.

text.traditional: 高雄好玩嗎？
text.simplified: 高雄好玩嗎？
text.pinyin: Gāoxióng hǎowán ma?
text.english: Was Kaohsiung fun?

text.traditional: 很好玩，我坐了三個半小時的火車，下了火車就坐捷運去西子灣了，那裡風景很漂亮。
text.simplified: 很好玩，我坐了三個半小時的火車，下了火車就坐捷運去西子灣了，那裡風景很漂亮。
text.pinyin: Hěn hǎowán, wǒ zuò le sān ge bàn xiǎoshí de huǒchē, xià le huǒchē jiù zuò jiéyùn qù Xīzǐwān le, nàlǐ fēngjǐng hěn piàoliàng.
text.english: Very fun! I took the train for three and a half hours, and as soon as I got off the train, I took the MRT to Sizihwan. The scenery there was gorgeous.

text.traditional: 你應該搭高鐵去，這樣更快，只需要一個半小時。
text.simplified: 你應該搭高鐵去，這樣更快，只需要一個半小時。
text.pinyin: Nǐ yīnggāi dā gāotiě qù, zhèyàng gèng kuài, zhǐ xūyào yí ge bàn xiǎoshí.
text.english: You should have taken the High Speed Rail (HSR); it’s much faster, taking only an hour and a half.

text.traditional: 好，我下次一定要坐高鐵。你呢？這次旅行怎麼樣？
text.simplified: 好，我下次一定要坐高鐵。你呢？這次旅行怎麼樣？
text.pinyin: Hǎo, wǒ xià cì yídìng yào zuò gāotiě. Nǐ ne? Zhè cì lǚxíng zěnmeyàng?
text.english: All right, I'll definitely take the HSR next time. How about you? How was your trip?

text.traditional: 我玩得很開心，可是旅館的房間有點問題，浴室沒有水。
text.simplified: 我玩得很開心，可是旅館的房間有點問題，浴室沒有水。
text.pinyin: Wǒ wán de hěn kāixīn, kěshì lǚguǎn de fángjiān yǒudiǎn wèntí, yùshì méiyǒu shuǐ.
text.english: I had a great time, but there was a problem with the hotel room: the bathroom had no water.

text.traditional: 沒有水？那你怎麼洗澡？
text.simplified: 沒有水？那你怎麼洗澡？
text.pinyin: Méiyǒu shuǐ? Nà nǐ zěnme xǐzǎo?
text.english: No water? Then how did you take a shower?

text.traditional: 後來我換了房間，旅館老闆說付一半的錢就好了。
text.simplified: 後來我換了房間，旅館老闆說付一半的錢就好了。
text.pinyin: Hòulái wǒ huàn le fángjiān, lǚguǎn lǎobǎn shuō fù yíbàn de qián jiù hǎo le.
text.english: Later I changed rooms, and the hotel owner said paying half price was fine.

text.traditional: 合歡山下雪了嗎？冷不冷？
text.simplified: 合歡山下雪了嗎？冷不冷？
text.pinyin: Héhuān Shān xiàxuě le ma? Lěng bù lěng?
text.english: Did it snow on Hehuanshan? Was it cold?

text.traditional: 下雪了，很冷，風也很大，可是很好玩。你看，這是我照的相片。
text.simplified: 下雪了，很冷，風也很大，可是很好玩。你看，這是我照的相片。
text.pinyin: Xiàxuě le, hěn lěng, fēng yě hěn dà, kěshì hěn hǎowán. Nǐ kàn, zhè shì wǒ zhào de xiàngpiàn.
text.english: It did snow. It was very cold, and the wind was strong, but it was really fun. Look, these are photos I took.

text.traditional: 你笑得好開心，風景真漂亮！
text.simplified: 你笑得好開心，風景真漂亮！
text.pinyin: Nǐ xiào de hǎo kāixīn, fēngjǐng zhēn piàoliàng!
text.english: You're smiling so happily, and the scenery is really beautiful!
